sprint: Magic Publish — Sprint M1 (Foundation). The first sprint of the approved nine-sprint roadmap in docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md: "Introduce Magic Publish as a new publish capability without changing existing publishing behaviour. No UI changes. No renderer modifications. No animation yet."
task: New js/magicReveal.js owns the reveal contract — revealStages(slide) -> [{slide,label,holdMs}] — a pure function of the FINAL saved page, no history, no timeline, nothing hooked into autosave or AppState (docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md §0: the reveal is a choreographed decomposition of the finished page, not a record of what a child actually did). It never mutates the slide it is handed, which is what lets it run during Publish with zero risk to the page the child is looking at. M1 ships the contract only: one Finished stage, so Magic Publish produces a real, working, deliberately non-magical video end to end; M2 fills in Blank -> World -> Artwork -> Decorations -> Text -> Finished behind the same signature with no plumbing changes downstream. The Magic Creation destination joins REGISTRY in js/storyDestinations.js alongside BOOK/CAROUSEL/REEL — id 'magic', one 1080x1920 vertical format, its own publishMessages/finishingMessage/progressNoun 'Scene'. One genuine design tension resolved: the pipeline calls createCanvas/renderPage/encodePage once per PAGE but a reveal is many FRAMES per page, so renderPage honours the contract (draws the finished page into the supplied canvas) while encodePage returns {frames:[...]} and finish() flattens every page's frames into one list for ReelComposer — PublishStudio needed no changes at all, it treats a payload as opaque. Frames render through the SAME SlideRenderer pipeline the editor/Book/Carousel/Reel already use (Rule 5), so the reveal can never show authoring chrome: the editor is not involved at any point. Audio is deliberately absent until M7 (narration -> ambient -> silence); ReelComposer feeds its own silent track for the whole recording, so a soundless reveal composes correctly today. Verified 32/32 via magic_m1_verify: the MagicReveal contract including the no-mutation guarantee and the null/undefined cases; the registry (all four destinations present, every one validating cleanly, magic non-comingSoon with all four hooks); the destination grid (real card, no Coming Soon chip, format pickable, Continue enables); a full 2-page publish reaching Celebration with a real video blob checked at the byte level (>20KB, video/*, _magic.webm, EBML magic bytes 0x1A45DFA3); the presentation hooks (Scene progress noun, 'Watch The Magic'); and the regression that matters most — Story Book still publishes a real PDF after M1. One test-methodology bug found and fixed in the suite, not an app bug: validate() takes ONE destination and deliberately reports duplicate-id for anything already in REGISTRY (that rule exists for register()), so each is probed under a non-colliding id. Regression: reel 15/15, reel_backdrop 10/10, reel_pageturn 12/12, voice_note 22/22, voice 16/16, both goldenBuilds PASS. Cache-bust ?v=0346 -> ?v=0347.
